URL: (compiled) Monday 12 October 2026 EVENING ticker basis
Primary: CNBC quote endpoint, read 17:42 BST. Cross-check: Trading Economics (UK 10Y, Brent, US 10Y, GB100).

*** THE GULF PREMIUM ARRIVED DURING THE SESSION — THIS MORNING'S READING IS REVERSED ***
This morning's edition published Brent at 103.93, DOWN 0.75%, and said plainly that the market was
"setting the Russian diesel supply against the Gulf risk and finding them close to cancelling out".
By the close Brent is 106.68, UP 1.87% — a swing of about 2.6% in under ten hours, and now above
Friday's settle rather than below it. The morning reading was correct when written and is now out of
date; the honest account is that the premium took most of a session to arrive, not that it never came.
What arrived with it: a reported drone attack on an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz region, Iranian
forces targeting what Al Jazeera calls a "US-UAE oil shuttle" moving crude beyond the strait, and a
Saudi minister vowing a "serious response" to the airport attacks. Oil company chiefs stayed away from
an energy congress in Riyadh.
BRENT CROSS-CHECK: Trading Economics 106.63 +1.83% against CNBC 106.68 +1.87%. Agreement on level to
0.05 and on direction. WTI on TE 93.64 +1.95%.

*** THE GILT BASIS FIX FROM THIS MORNING IS CONFIRMED — INDEPENDENTLY ***
This morning resolved a six-day dispute by establishing that Friday's TRUE close was ~5.4226 (CNBC's
post-17:00 read), not the 5.4396 we had read at 18:15 on Friday and published as 5.44. Tonight:
  CNBC live:         5.4444
  5.4444 - 5.4226 = +0.0218 -> +0.02
  Trading Economics: UK 10Y 5.44, day change +0.020%, dated Oct/12.
TE's independently computed day change is +0.020 against our +0.0218. That is agreement to within a
fifth of a basis point, and it confirms the corrected Friday basis rather than the old one. Had we
still been using 5.4396 the computed change would have been +0.005, which TE would have contradicted.
The rule from this morning stands and is now evidenced: take the gilt from the post-17:00 value, never
from an 18:00-18:15 quote, and corroborate with the TE daily change.
CNBC's own previous_day_closing read 5.4466 tonight — an intraday value again, unusable for the
seventh consecutive day.

*** NOT LIVE: US TREASURIES ***
US10Y returned 5.242% stamped 2026-10-09T17:01 EDT and US30Y 5.60% stamped the same day. Trading
Economics also still dates US 10Y to Oct/09. BOTH providers are stale on the same instrument, so this
is the source's lag and not a one-provider fault. The Treasury therefore carries Friday's close with
Friday's move (+0.01), declared, exactly as this morning. Note .SPX and .VIX ARE live (12:42 EDT), so
this is specific to the bond feed, not to US markets generally.

*** BITCOIN: THE WEEKEND BASIS IS RETIRED TONIGHT, AND SAYING SO MATTERS ***
Through Saturday, Sunday and this morning, bitcoin was measured against FRIDAY's close (82,322.43)
because every other instrument on the ticker was shut and a Friday basis kept the series continuous.
Normal sessions have now resumed, so each instrument reverts to its own previous close — which for
bitcoin is Sunday's (83,618.42), giving 82,747.30 = -1.04%.
On the retired Friday-close basis bitcoin would read +0.52% tonight. Both are defensible; what is not
defensible is switching silently, so the change is recorded here. A reader comparing with this
morning's +2.19 is seeing a basis change as well as a price fall.

FTSE CROSS-CHECK: Trading Economics GB100 10,656.28 +0.99%, identical to CNBC to the penny, stamped
Oct/12. The feed lag that affects the first half-hour after the open is absent at the close, for the
seventh evening running — the diagnosis holds.
